brief.subject: Diesel jumps 7.6 cents; Schneider moves eastern rail to NS
brief.headline: Diesel Climbs to $6.352 as Schneider Shifts Eastern Rail Business to Norfolk Southern
brief.dek: Diesel rises 7.6 cents, Schneider picks Norfolk Southern over CSX, Mexico truckers pause strike, and the Fed holds rates.
brief.lede: Diesel rose 7.6 cents last week to $6.352 a gallon, a fresh squeeze on cash flow for small carriers.

sections.heading: Diesel jumps 7.6 cents
bullets: $6.352 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-10-26.
Up 7.6 cents (1.2%) week over week, so check that fuel surcharges are keeping pace.
Still down 3.0 cents over four weeks, but the one-week spike hits margins right away.

sections.heading: Schneider swaps CSX for Norfolk Southern
bullets: Schneider is making Norfolk Southern its primary eastern rail provider, replacing CSX.
The move comes as Norfolk Southern pursues a merger with Union Pacific, which could reshape eastern intermodal lanes.
Schneider raised its outlook despite a slight Q3 miss, a sign that big fleets see demand holding.

sections.heading: Mexico truckers pause national strike
bullets: Mexican trucking leaders have temporarily suspended their nationwide strike over deadly highway crime.
They say talks must deliver measurable security gains, so cross-border disruptions could return.

sections.heading: Shipper and LTL signals
bullets: 11% was the jump in Amazon's Q3 shipping costs, driven by higher fuel and linehaul expenses.
FedEx Freight says LTL volumes are stabilizing and expects Q4 margins to improve.
FedEx expects a strong peak season, a possible boost for spot demand.
Covenant's Q3 revenue rose 19.2% to $353.9 million, led by growth in managed freight.

sections.heading: Rates, rail and new freight nodes
bullets: The Fed held its main rate steady despite accelerating inflation, so equipment financing costs stay put for now.
26,000 containers a year are targeted to move off the road by Georgia's new inland rail hub, which could cut local drayage.
$400M Walmart distribution center in Cibolo, Texas, is set to break ground this February.
